name: PostHog Feature Flags
description: PostHog Feature Flags supports controlled feature rollout, multivariate releases, targeting, experimentation, and remote configuration within PostHog projects.
agentUseSummary: Connect a dedicated project-scoped personal API key with only feature_flag:read, select the US or EU Cloud region, and bind one non-production project. Relay approval-gates a 25-item active flag list and one exact redacted flag read; targeting properties, cohorts, evaluation, payloads, and all mutations remain blocked.

credentialRequirements.name: POSTHOG_FEATURE_FLAGS_PERSONAL_API_KEY
credentialRequirements.label: PostHog personal API key
credentialRequirements.helpText: Use a dedicated project-scoped personal API key with only feature_flag:read.

credentialRequirements.name: POSTHOG_FEATURE_FLAGS_REGION
credentialRequirements.label: PostHog Cloud region
credentialRequirements.helpText: Enter exactly us or eu. Self-hosted origins are outside V1.

credentialRequirements.name: POSTHOG_FEATURE_FLAGS_PROJECT_ID
credentialRequirements.label: PostHog project ID
credentialRequirements.helpText: Bind Relay to one non-production numeric project.

capabilities.label: Read feature flags
capabilities.description: Read bounded, redacted feature-flag configuration with approval.

approvalRequired.label: Read PostHog feature flags
approvalRequired.description: Read bounded active flag summaries or one exact redacted flag configuration.

blocked.label: Expose credentials
blocked.description: Personal API keys, Bearer headers, stored project routing, and credential-bearing fields never enter agent-visible inputs or results.

blocked.label: Read targeting data
blocked.description: Person/group properties, distinct IDs, cohort membership, condition values, evaluation contexts, remote-config payloads, and evaluation results are excluded.

blocked.label: Mutate PostHog
blocked.description: Flag creation, updates, deletes, archival, rollout changes, experiments, cohort creation, bulk actions, test evaluation, dashboards, and all other mutations remain provider-side.

blocked.label: Use arbitrary APIs
blocked.description: Only the official feature-flag list and exact integer retrieve routes run on enumerated US/EU private API origins with stored project binding; arbitrary paths, queries, pagination, public evaluation endpoints, local evaluation, exports, and raw API access are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: Both bounded feature-flag reads require approval; exact region/project binding, response bounds, audits, targeting redaction, and evaluation/mutation blocks remain enforced.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: The selected redacted feature-flag read runs without Relay per-action approval; exact region/project binding, response bounds, audits, targeting redaction, and evaluation/mutation blocks remain enforced.

runtimeSupport.description: Railway attaches the encrypted read-scoped key server-side and mounts two project-bound, approval-gated, redacted flag reads.
Railway attaches the encrypted read-scoped key server-side and mounts two project-bound, approval-gated, redacted flag reads.

providerSetup.blocker: PostHog requires a customer project and a dedicated personal API key restricted to feature_flag:read and that project. No console, account, key, project, flag, Railway environment, or deployment is allowed in this worker.
providerSetup.nextAction: Create a dedicated project-scoped feature_flag:read key outside this worker, configure its encrypted value, US/EU region and project ID in Railway staging, then verify project binding, active-list and exact-read redaction, approval/access denial, response bounds, rate limiting, key revocation, pause/disconnect, and post-disconnect denial.

evidence.supports: PostHog's official OpenAPI pins GET /api/projects/{project_id}/feature_flags/ and GET /api/projects/{project_id}/feature_flags/{id}/ to feature_flag:read; write routes require feature_flag:write, and list supports active, limit and offset.

PostHog documents US/EU private API origins, personal-key authentication for private endpoints, pagination, rate limiting, and the distinction between private metadata APIs and public flag evaluation.
PostHog documents Bearer authentication, project/access scoping, least-privilege scopes, secret handling, individual invalidation, and key rotation.
